title: Sales Enablement: Prospect Playbook - Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook is a consolidated sales enablement reference for enterprise and prospect-facing conversations. It combines positioning and messaging, competitive talking points, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, short case studies tailored for enterprise buyers, and a security FAQ targeted at technical procurement teams. Use this document during discovery calls, solution workshops, and executive briefings.

Audience
- AEs, SEs, Sales Engineers, Solutions Architects, Customer Success, and Growth SDRs.
- Primary use: prospect meetings, RFP responses, and POC design discussions.

1) Core positioning and messaging (TL;DR)
- One-liner: Redwood Inference - a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- 3 core pillars customers care about:
  - Production-first performance: low p50/p95 latency, predictable throughput, and autoscaling for burst workloads.
  - Cost & control: batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles that reduce per-token unit economics.
  - Deployment flexibility & compliance: hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads.

Key user-facing messages (by persona)
- Engineering/Platform: "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; optimized runtime for GPU kernels and KV cache; programmatic rollout controls and tracing hooks."
- Product/ML teams: "Quality-safe rollouts, integrated evals/regression alerts, and model catalog with recommended quantization profiles to preserve quality while lowering cost."
- Security/Compliance: "Customer-managed VPC option, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and SOC2-ready controls - designed for regulated workloads."
- Procurement/Finance: "Clear unit economics, predictable reserved capacity pricing, and tooling to quantify cost savings from batching and caching."

Elevator pitch (30s)
- "Redwood Inference is an inference platform that lets you ship LLM features with predictable latency and unit economics across cloud or private deployment. Customers use a single API and tooling set to reduce per-token cost, maintain quality safeguards, and meet security requirements without building an inference stack."

2) Competitive brief (talking points + comparison table)
- Main competitor categories: Managed cloud AI endpoints (big cloud providers), LLM API vendors (simplicity-first), and self-hosted inference vendors (infrastructure-first).

Competitive comparison (high-level):
| Capability | Redwood Inference | Big Cloud AI Endpoints | LLM API Vendors | Inference Infra Vendors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private) | ✓ | Partial (hosted + cloud-only dedicated) | Mostly hosted only | Self-hosted only |
| Production performance controls (batching, cache, runtime kernels) | ✓ (built-in) | Limited | Limited | Varies; requires ops work |
| Cost transparency & tooling | Unit economics + Optimize toolkit | Often opaque | Usage-only pricing | Customer-built |
| Security & compliance (VPC/KMS/audit logs) | Enterprise-grade private + integrations | Good (cloud-native) | Limited | Depends on vendor |
| Rollouts & safety (evals + regressions) | First-class (integrated) | Limited | Minimal | Tooling required |

Competitive talking points / objections
- If buyer is considering cloud provider: emphasize cross-environment consistency and better unit economics for sustained inference workloads (reserved capacity + batching).
- If buyer is considering API-first vendor: emphasize SLA, latency targets, and enterprise controls for data residency and private deployment.
- If buyer is evaluating infra vendors: highlight reduced engineering lift and integrated evals/quality monitoring - we provide the runtime and operational stack without shipping a full infra team.

3) Pricing guidance (prospect-level framing)
- Offer tiers: Hosted API (usage-based), Dedicated (monthly/annual reserved capacity contracts), Private (platform license + support).
- How to position: start with Hosted for trial/POC; recommend Dedicated when steady-state >= expected monthly token / concurrent throughput threshold; propose Private for regulated or air-gapped environments.

Sample pricing table (for buyer conversations)
| Pricing component | Typical buyer signal | Sales tilt | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hosted API (usage) | Low volume / proof-of-concept | Fast onboarding, free credits | Per-token + per-embedding; good for evaluations and startup usage |
| Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) | Predictable throughput / cost-sensitive | Offer 6-12 month commit with burst capacity | Price by reserved GPUs + support; add autoscale buffers and SLOs in contract |
| Private (VPC / On-prem) | Regulated / data residency needs | Enterprise licensing + services | Platform fee + annual support; include onboarding & runbook services |

Sizing rules of thumb (talking points for SEs)
- Recommend Dedicated when sustained throughput > 1M tokens/day or sustained concurrency > 10 r/s with p95 latency targets under 500ms.
- Example TCO conversation: show cost impact of batching (20-40% token cost reduction) and KV caching (cost-effective for repeated prefixes like chat history). Use Redwood Optimize outputs when available.

Negotiation levers
- Duration of reserved commit (6/12/24 months), support tier, observability retention (logs/trace retention), and white-glove onboarding professional services.

4) Pitch Deck outline (7-10 slides; SE notes included)
- Slide 0: Cover - Customer name, meeting title, presenter names and roles.
- Slide 1: Business problem & opportunity - Quantify user impact and costs of current approach.
- Slide 2: Why Redwood (3 pillars) - Performance, cost & control, deployment flexibility.
- Slide 3: Architecture overview - hosted / dedicated / private options, routing, caching overview. (Include diagram: API -> Router -> Serving runtime (GPU pools) -> KV cache -> Metrics & Audit).
- Slide 4: Demo / POC plan - goals, success criteria, timeline, data access & security controls.
- Slide 5: Pricing & commercial options - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, example TCO.
- Slide 6: Security & compliance - KMS integrations, VPC, audit logging, SOC2 / penetration testing cadence.
- Slide 7: Case study highlights - 2 concise examples with specific outcomes (latency, cost savings, reliability).
- Slide 8: Next steps & ask - POC timeline, technical contacts, procurement contacts.

Deck notes for SEs
- Bring pre-computed TCOs for 3 scenarios: POC, scale to 100k users, and enterprise steady-state.
- Provide a short demo script that shows p95 latency on a sample prompt set, and a fallback behavior in a model variant scenario.

5) Case studies (2 short vignettes to use in pitch)
- Case Study A - AI-native SaaS (Customer: AcmeAssist)
  - Problem: Chat feature suffering from unpredictable latency and high token costs.
  - Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated, enabled KV caching for conversation prefixes, applied quantization profile Q4_8 for a moderate quality-cost tradeoff.
  - Outcome: 35% reduction in per-token cost, p95 latency reduced from 720ms to 380ms, 99.95% availability over a 3-month period.
  - Owner: Growth customer reference (contact: rina.sato@redwood.ai)

- Case Study B - Regulated Financial Services (Customer: FinSecure)
  - Problem: Data residency and auditability required for model inference on sensitive customer data.
  - Solution: Deployed Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS, audit logging to SIEM, and SOC2 attestation evidence package delivered.
  - Outcome: Successful internal audit sign-off; 0 security findings related to inference layer; accelerated pilot to production in 10 weeks.
  - Owner: Enterprise sales (contact: miguel.ortiz@redwood.ai)

6) Security FAQ for prospects (technical answers for RFPs & procurement)
- Q: Where does customer data go when using the Hosted API?
  - A: By default, inference requests are processed in the chosen region; logs and payloads are retained according to contract/plan. For enterprise customers we offer options to disable payload retention or route to Private/Dedicated environments. See Data Retention table below.

- Q: What encryption is used in transit and at rest?
  - A: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for stored artifacts. KMS integrations allow customer-managed keys (CMKs) for encryption-at-rest.

- Q: Do you support customer-managed KMS / HSM?
  - A: Yes. Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed KMS integrations; On-prem packages can integrate with on-prem HSMs.

- Q: How do you handle data residency and on-prem requirements?
  - A: Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) provide full data residency guarantees. Hosted API supports regional processing and contractual commitments for residency.

- Q: What compliance certifications do you maintain?
  - A: SOC 2 Type II (in-scope for inference platform), annual penetration tests, and internal security review process. For specific audits we provide an evidence package and sign NDA.

- Q: Can you disable telemetry / logs for a customer?
  - A: Telemetry and debug logs can be disabled or configured for restricted retention in Dedicated/Private contracts. For Hosted we offer a limited-retention plan and can negotiate custom retention as part of enterprise agreements.

- Q: How do you support separation of duties and RBAC?
  - A: Role-based access control with SSO (SAML/OIDC), fine-grained permissions per environment, and audit trails. We can map to customer IAM during Private deployments.

Data retention and access table (example)
| Data type | Hosted (default) | Hosted (enterprise) | Dedicated | Private / On-prem |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Request payloads | 30 days (default) | configurable / off | configurable | customer-managed |
| Audit logs | 90 days | configurable | configurable | customer-managed |
| Model artifacts | Immutable | Immutable | Immutable | Managed by customer |

7) Demo & POC checklist (technical and commercial pre-reqs)
- Technical pre-reqs:
  1. Sample prompt set and expected success criteria (accuracy, latency).
  2. Access to a test dataset (or synthetic equivalent) with expected size and payload distribution.
  3. Network allowlist (IP ranges) and credentials for SSO/KMS where applicable.
  4. Contact list: technical lead, security lead, procurement contact.
- Commercial pre-reqs:
  1. POC acceptance criteria and rolling success definition.
  2. Temporary eval license or hosted credits.
  3. NDA if exchanging sensitive data.

8) Objection handling cheatsheet (top 6 objections)
- "We can run this in-house cheaper" - Lead with total cost of ownership: highlight engineering effort, ongoing ops, and Redwood Optimize savings from batching/caching. Offer a POC to model TCO.
- "We can't send data to a third party" - Walk through Private deployment and KMS on-prem options. Provide SOC2 + evidence package.
- "Latency is critical" - Provide p95 latency benchmarks for similar customers and propose a Dedicated sizing + autoscale policy aligned to latency SLOs.
- "We're locked into cloud provider tooling" - Emphasize consistent API & toolchain: migrate workloads with minimal refactor; we provide integration consulting.
- "Pricing is opaque" - Offer usage examples and a concrete TCO workbook; include configurable Dedicated proposals.
- "We need long-term roadmap alignment" - Share product roadmap and customer advisory board cadence; propose a joint roadmap session.

9) Owners, contacts, and next steps
- Playbook owner: Go-to-Market Enablement (owner: aisha.patel@redwood.ai).
- SE on-call: #se-oncall (Slack).
- Enterprise AE contact (ESD): miguel.ortiz@redwood.ai.
- Deal packaging lead (pricing questions): pricing@redwood.ai.

Next steps for AE/SE before first customer meeting
1. Tailor the pitch deck to the prospect vertical and include one relevant case study.
2. Run Redwood Optimize for a quick cost projection if prospect can share sample load.
3. Confirm security pre-reqs and determine whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the recommended path.

Appendix: Useful snippets
- Command to run a small latency test (example):
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-2026","input":"Say hello"}'

- Example POC timeline (4 weeks):
  - Week 0: NDA, scope, and data access
  - Week 1: Initial integration, baseline benchmarking
  - Week 2: Optimization (batching, caching, quantization)
  - Week 3: Feature validation and handoff to CSM
  - Week 4: Executive review and FR/POC acceptance
